title: Structured Credit and Implied Correlation

maps.tested: The sheet flags one LO for the impact table and one concept as likely testable, while recommending you do this reading last because of its time cost.
maps.specifics: Named: LO 40.i, 'just remember the impacts via the table', with one possible calculation; and the concept of implied correlation, described as 'likely to be testable.' Reported independently as 'Gaussian copula, implied correlation.'

vardeezReading: Important: LO 40.i is an important LO where you should just remember the impacts via the table, one calculation question can come from the reading but it should be left to the very end because it consumes time, and the concept of implied correlation (LO 40.l) seems likely to be testable.

los.vardeez: Remember the impacts via the table; one calculation question possible

selectors.name: Impacts table: default probability and correlation
selectors.what: How a higher default probability and a higher default correlation move the equity, mezzanine and senior tranches: higher default probability hurts every tranche; higher correlation helps the equity and hurts the senior, and the mezzanine behaves like the senior at low default rates and like the equity at high ones.

selectors.name: Read tranche values off simulation grid
selectors.what: The one possible calculation: read tranche values, writedowns or losses off the simulation grid (the 1,000 threads of 100 loans) at given default probability and correlation, or compute a tranche Credit VaR from the simulated values (equity: par minus the 10th lowest value at 99%; bonds: the 10th highest loss minus EL).
selectors.theory: How the simulation works: default times from correlated normals with hazard rate lambda = -log(1 - pi), defaults counted per year and passed through the waterfall; why the tranche writedown depends on the correlation (mezzanine writedown rises with correlation at low pi and falls at high pi) and why the equity Credit VaR can fall as pi and rho rise.

selectors.name: Implied correlation from a tranche price
selectors.what: Back out the implied correlation: the unique copula correlation at which the modelled tranche value, using risk-neutral PDs from CDS spreads and risk-free discounting, equals the market price; or read the change in implied correlation from a change in the tranche price at unchanged PDs.
selectors.theory: A rising equity tranche price with unchanged PDs means implied correlation has risen (Malz: equity at 5.0 with 2% PD matches rho = 0.3, 5.6 means rho = 0.6), a higher market assessment of systematic risk; inputs are risk-neutral, not physical, and the concept is as much market risk as credit risk.

selectors.name: Gaussian copula and implied correlation
selectors.what: The Gaussian copula as the model that links single-name default probabilities through one pairwise correlation, and implied correlation as the copula correlation inferred from standard tranche prices, tied to the tranche's attachment point (base correlation) and varying across tranches (correlation skew).

notSelected: CR-22 j (default01, the change in tranche value per 1 bp rise in default probability) and CR-22 k (risk factors: systematic risk, thin tranches, granularity, prepayment) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; CR-22 a to g and m are covered by topic A9.
